## inputs — Grade C+

- [ ] **Major** · both · 360px — InputGroupedIconsExample (the segmented `|< <` 'Page number' `> >|` control) overflows the viewport at 360px in both light and dark. The control is full-bleed with no side margin and the rightmost skip-to-end (`>|`) button is clipped off the right screen edge, so the group is visibly cut. It needs to wrap, scroll, or shrink cells to fit mobile rather than run past the edge.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Section headers render as run-together uppercase strings with heavy letter-spacing and no word boundaries ('INPUTBOTHSIDEICONSEXAMPLE', 'INPUTWITHLABELANDMESSAGEDEMO', 'INPUTGROUPEDICONSEXAMPLE'). They read as one unbroken word and hurt scan-ability. Demo names should be split into words (e.g. 'Input Both Side Icons'). Systemic across all three groups.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Inconsistent horizontal alignment between demos: Search username, Page number and the error field are center-aligned, while InputWithLabelAndMessage / InputWithLabel left-align inside an indented column. Worse, in InputWithLabelDemo the 'Label' caption is indented to the right of the input box's own left edge, so label and field don't share a left margin. Pick one alignment system.
- [ ] **Minor** · dark · all widths — Dark-theme input fills are near-black with no visible border, so the Email Address, Label and 'Set antena number' fields nearly dissolve into the black page background. There is no clear field boundary; a subtle border or a one-step-lighter fill would give the inputs a defined edge the way a designed dark theme would.
- [ ] **Polish** · both · all widths — Fields look flat with no apparent focus, hover, or press affordance (no ring, no elevation change). For a premium input set at least a focus ring / border-color shift should be evident. Also a content typo: placeholder reads 'Set antena number' (antenna).

## checkboxes — Grade C

- [ ] **Major** · dark · all widths — In dark theme the unchecked checkbox squares are almost invisible: both the CheckboxCards control (top-right of Toys/Books/Clothes/Games) and every checkbox in the Coffee list render as a near-black square on a near-black surface with no discernible border. Users can't see there's a control to tap. Needs a visible unchecked border/fill contrast in dark.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — The CheckboxList 'Coffee' card uses a heavy solid ~2px border (pure black in light, pure white in dark) that clashes with the soft, low-contrast rounded borders of the CheckboxCards directly above it. The two demos look like they come from different design systems; the stark border reads as unrefined/hardcoded rather than a designed surface.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · 1280px — On desktop the Coffee card is a fixed narrow ~360px column centered on the page, leaving large empty dead space on both sides, while the CheckboxCards above render full-width. The inconsistent demo width makes the section feel unbalanced at 1280.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · 360px — At 360px the Coffee card's border sits flush against the left and right viewport edges with no side margin, so the heavy border looks clipped/cramped against the screen edges instead of inset like a card.
- [ ] **Polish** · dark · all widths — Card borders in dark are so subtle that the four CheckboxCards read as flat, with weak separation and no elevation. The colored category pills (Toys/Books/Clothes/Games) also look muddy and desaturated in dark rather than intentionally re-toned. Content typo: 'Cappucino' should be 'Cappuccino'.

## radiogroups — Grade F

- [ ] **Broken** · both · all widths — The entire radiogroups group crashes. All four screenshots (light/dark, 360/1280) show a full-screen red React error overlay 'Error 1 of 1 - useGroupMedia: No parent group "window" found.' with a call stack useGroupMedia -> RadioList -> react-stack-bottom-frame. No radio component renders at all. Root cause: RadioList calls useGroupMedia against a Tamagui group named 'window' that isn't provided in this harness; RadioList must define its own named group (or the audit page must wrap it in a group name="window") before it can render.

## switches — Grade F

- [ ] **Broken** · light+dark · 360+1280 (all four variants) — Entire switches page is replaced by the dev error overlay in all four screenshots (light/dark, 360/1280). Thrown error: 'TypeError: Failed to set an indexed property [0] on CSSStyleDeclaration: Indexed property setter is not supported', via setValueForStyle -> setValueForStyles -> setProp -> setInitialProperties -> completeWork during render. No switch renders; the group is completely unusable. Root cause is almost certainly a style value shaped as an indexed/array object (numeric '0' key) reaching React DOM's inline style writer — e.g. an array/spread passed to a style prop, or an array-valued transform on the switch track/thumb. Fix at the switch component's style prop before any visual review is possible.

## textareas — Grade B-

- [ ] **Major** · dark · 360+1280 — The filled textarea fields lose almost all contrast against the page in dark mode. The AvatarOutContentAction and TitleContentMessage fields render as a near-black surface (~#0d0d0d) on the near-black (#000) page, so the input boundary is barely perceptible and the field reads as 'not there'. In light mode the same fields have a clear light-gray fill that reads as an obvious input. Dark needs a lighter surface token or a visible 1px border so the field boundary is legible.
- [ ] **Major** · light+dark · 360+1280 — Placeholder text renders at full-contrast bold, so empty fields look pre-filled. 'Write your comment' (AvatarNameContentAction and AvatarOutContentAction) and 'Your text here' (TitleContentMessage) appear as solid black (light) / solid white (dark) heading-weight text rather than a muted placeholder, killing the 'type here' affordance. Only the WritePreviewAction field uses a correct muted gray placeholder ('Your comment here...'). Standardize on one muted placeholder color across all four variants.
- [ ] **Minor** · light+dark · 360+1280 — AvatarNameContentAction (first card) has no visible textarea boundary at all: 'Write your comment' floats in the card body with empty space below it and only a divider line above the action bar, giving zero affordance that the region is an editable multi-line input. The other three variants all use a filled/bordered container, so this one is inconsistent and unclear.
- [ ] **Polish** · light+dark · 360+1280 — No hover/press/focus affordance is evident on the fields or the icon buttons. The share and file/copy icon buttons in the AvatarNameContentAction action bar are unlabeled and flat with no visible hit-area chrome; premium bar wants a clear focus ring on inputs and a hover state on the icon buttons.
- [ ] **Polish** · light+dark · 360+1280 — Gallery section labels are raw jammed variant names with no word spacing ('AVATARNAMECONTENTACTION', 'AVATAROUTCONTENTACTION', 'TITLECONTENTMESSAGE', 'WRITEPREVIEWACTION'). Reads like debug output rather than a premium showcase. (This is shared demo-page scaffolding, but it ships in the audit/gallery view.)

## layouts — Grade D

- [ ] **Broken** · light+dark · 360px — SignInRightImage does not collapse its two-column (form + hero image) grid on mobile. At 360px the right-hand laptop image stays in its column and overflows off the right screen edge while the form stays cramped in the left column, clipping every control: the email input shows 'email@exam[ple.com]', the password input shows 'Enter passw[ord]', and both social buttons are cut off as 'Continue with Git[hub]' and 'Continue with Face[book]'. The inputs are unreadable and effectively unusable. The grid must stack to a single column below a breakpoint (image above or below the form).
- [ ] **Major** · light+dark · 360px — As part of the same non-responsive block, the GitHub / Facebook social buttons and the 'Don't have an account? Sign up' link run full-bleed to the very left screen edge (x=0) with zero horizontal gutter, while the rest of the page keeps its inset. The block loses its page padding entirely on mobile.
- [ ] **Minor** · dark · 1280px — The ShortEmailPassword grouping container disappears in dark mode. In light/1280 there is a faint rounded card surface/shadow grouping the email, password and Back/Continue buttons; in dark/1280 there is no border or shadow, so the fields and buttons float ungrouped with no visible card. Add a subtle border or elevated surface token for the dark card.
- [ ] **Polish** · light+dark · 360+1280 — The laptop hero image in SignInRightImage carries a heavy yellow-to-orange-to-pink gradient tint that reads like a dated photo filter and feels less premium than the rest of the UI. The dark-theme darkening overlay is a nice designed-for-dark touch; it is the light-theme color tint that looks off. Consider a clean image or a subtle brand-consistent overlay instead.
- [ ] **Polish** · light+dark · 360+1280 — Same jammed-caps section labels as the other groups ('SHORTEMAILPASSWORD', 'SIGNINRIGHTIMAGE', 'SIGNINSCREEN') with no word spacing, reading like debug identifiers rather than a designed gallery heading.

## avatars — Grade B

- [ ] **Major** · both · 1280px — At 1280 every section's content is horizontally centered in the viewport while the section labels and full-width divider rules stay left-aligned at ~170px, leaving a ~450px empty left gutter. Content alignment also flips between breakpoints (left-aligned at 360, centered at 1280), so the label no longer visually anchors the avatars beneath it. HeroUI Pro would left-align the content under its label or use a real grid; the floating-center layout reads as unfinished.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · 360px — The CircularAvatars size samples (xs -> lg) are spaced with large, arbitrary gaps and the largest wraps to a second line, so the size progression doesn't read as an intentional scale. A consistent gap with the four sizes in one baseline-aligned row would make the scale legible.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Section labels render the camelCase source names as all-caps with letter-spacing and no word breaks (e.g. CIRCULARAVATARSWITHCUSTOMICONS, AVATARSGROUPED), producing unreadable run-on strings. Labels should be human-readable ('Circular avatars with custom icons').
- [ ] **Polish** · dark · all widths — In CircularAvatars the thin light ring around each avatar is barely perceptible against the near-black background, so avatars read as floating cutouts rather than deliberately bordered. A slightly stronger or theme-tuned ring would make the treatment feel designed for dark rather than inherited from light.
- [ ] **Polish** · both · all widths — RoundedAvatars use a very small corner radius that reads almost square and nearly identical to a sharp crop; a larger, consistent radius would distinguish the 'rounded' variant from the circular set and feel more deliberate.

## buttons — Grade C+

- [ ] **Major** · dark · all widths — The yellow 'Themed' button in dark mode renders as a muddy dark-olive/brown fill with dim yellow text, looking dirty and washed-out next to the cleaner navy, green and purple tints. The yellow (and to a lesser degree the orange) theme clearly wasn't tuned for dark; it reads as a naive HSL darken rather than a designed dark palette.
- [ ] **Major** · both · 1280px — Buttons keep a fixed ~330px width centered in the 1280 viewport instead of adapting, so the entire control column floats in the middle of a mostly empty page with huge margins on both sides. At 360 the same buttons are full-width. The desktop layout doesn't use the available space and looks unfinished versus a disciplined max-width/grid.
- [ ] **Major** · light · all widths — The pastel 'Themed' buttons put same-hue text on a pale tint of that hue; contrast is weakest on the yellow, orange, pink and green fills, where the 'Themed' label is hard to read. This falls below a premium legibility bar; the label color needs a darker/neutral tone or a stronger tint step.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — The Small and Normal size samples are nearly identical in height, so the Small/Normal/Big scale doesn't read as three distinct steps; only Big is visibly larger. Tighten Small so the size ramp is legible.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Section labels are unreadable run-on all-caps camelCase strings (BUTTONSWITHLEFTICONS, BUTTONSWITHLOADERS), same typography issue as the other groups.
- [ ] **Polish** · both · all widths — Neutral buttons (Active, Small, Normal, Big) are flat solid-gray fills with no border, shadow, or apparent hover/press affordance in the static render, so secondary hierarchy relies entirely on fill color. A subtle border, elevation, or state treatment would make them feel more premium and interactive.

## chips — Grade C+

- [ ] **Major** · light · all widths — ChipsNoTextColor renders white 'Input' text on pale pastel fills (white on light blue / light green / light pink), which is very low contrast and nearly illegible in light mode. It reads as a bug rather than a variant; the 'no text color' default needs to be a readable dark/auto-contrast token.
- [ ] **Major** · dark · all widths — In dark mode the six chip hues have uneven saturation and lightness: the blue is vivid and bright while the green and brown/orange are dark and muddy, and the maroon/purple sit in between. The set doesn't read as one deliberate palette; the hues need to be normalized to a consistent lightness/chroma target for dark.
- [ ] **Major** · both · 1280px — Same page-level layout problem as the other groups: at 1280 all chip rows are centered in the viewport while labels/rules are left-aligned, leaving a large empty left gutter and detaching the content from its label.
- [ ] **Minor** · dark · all widths — ChipsWithIcon in dark mode uses colored text and icon on a same-hue dark fill; the green 'Cake' on dark green and the brown 'Cake' on dark brown are low contrast and hard to read, whereas the blue reads fine. Contrast should be equalized across hues.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · 360px — Column count differs between chip sections at 360 (plain Chips wrap to a 3-up grid, the close-icon and icon variants wrap to 2-up), so the stacked sections don't share a column rhythm and left edges don't align consistently down the page.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Section labels are unreadable run-on all-caps camelCase (CHIPSNOTEXTCOLOR, CHIPSWITHCLOSEICON), consistent with the typography issue across groups.
- [ ] **Polish** · both · 360px — The close 'x' on ChipsWithCloseIcon is a small target inside an already-compact chip; at 360 it's near the minimum comfortable touch size. Enlarging the hit area (padding around the glyph) would improve mobile usability.

## datepickers — Grade B-

- [ ] **Major** · both · all widths — The Range/Single/Multiple segmented control has no visible selected-segment state. At 1280 the calendar is clearly in Range mode (two months shown), yet 'Range' reads identically to the inactive 'Single' and 'Multiple' labels: no pill, fill, or weight change. A segmented control with no active indicator leaves the user unable to tell which mode is on. Add a filled/elevated active segment.
- [ ] **Major** · both · 360px — Sibling inputs render at two different widths. DatePickerExample ('Select Date') and MonthPickerInput ('Select Month') are inset with side margins, while MultiSelectPicker ('Start date, End date') and RangePicker ('Start date - End date') stretch nearly edge-to-edge. Four controls that should form a consistent stack instead step between two widths, which reads as a layout bug at 360.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · 1280px — Alignment disconnect at desktop: the calendar card, the toggle, and every input are centered in a ~640px column, but the section labels (CALENDAR, DATEPICKEREXAMPLE, RANGEPICKER) sit flush-left against the far margin. The label and its control don't share an edge, leaving a large dead gutter and an unanchored, un-designed feel. HeroUI Pro would left-align the control to its label or place the label above a max-width container.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Inconsistent trailing-icon treatment across the date inputs. 'Select Date' and 'Select Month' wrap the calendar glyph in a distinctly shaded box (a button-in-input look), whereas the MultiSelect and Range inputs render the same glyph flush with no box. Pick one icon treatment for all date fields.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — No 'today' indicator on the calendar. The current date (July 9/10 2026) is unmarked and reads the same as every other day cell. Premium calendars ring or tint today for orientation.
- [ ] **Polish** · dark · all widths — Dark calendar day cells are uniform white numerals with no visible hover or selected affordance, so the grid feels flat and the selected-day contrast can't be established. Design an explicit dark selected state (accent fill + readable foreground) and a subtle hover so cells feel interactive rather than static text.
- [ ] **Polish** · both · all widths — The inputs are flat two-tone bars (lighter icon box on a gray/near-black field) with no border definition, elevation, or focus ring shown. They look generic rather than premium; a crisper border, consistent radius, and a defined focus/hover state would lift them.

## dialogs — Grade C+

- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — SlidingPopoverDemo renders three bare icons (crown, waves, moon) with no button background, border, hit-area, or label. They read as decorative glyphs, not interactive triggers, so there is zero affordance that tapping them opens anything. Give them a real button/toggle treatment and labels or tooltips.
- [ ] **Minor** · dark · all widths — In dark mode the 'Open Alert' / 'Open Alert 2' buttons are dark gray on near-black with a nearly invisible edge. They barely separate from the page background. Raise the surface color or add a defined border so the buttons read as tappable elements against the black canvas.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Buttons are generic flat gray pills with no icon, elevation, or primary/secondary hierarchy. The iOS-style pair 'Open Alert' and 'Open Alert 2' are visually identical, giving no hint they trigger different dialogs. Differentiate them (primary vs secondary styling, or an icon).
- [ ] **Minor** · both · 1280px — At 1280 the page is a handful of small centered buttons in a vast empty canvas with no framing, preview, or context for what each dialog produces. The showcase reads as sparse/unfinished. A card or preview frame per demo would give it structure.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Coverage gap: the dialogs/alerts are never captured in their open state, so the actual modal styling, overlay/scrim, spacing, corner radius, and dark-mode treatment of the alert body cannot be judged from these screenshots. The dialog content is the whole point of the group and needs an opened-state capture to audit. This grade covers only the visible triggers.

## pickers — Grade C+

- [ ] **Major** · dark · all widths — Dark mode: the dashed dropzone borders for both ImagePicker and UploadFile are extremely low-contrast (very dark gray dashes on near-black) and nearly disappear. The drop-target boundary is the core visual of a dropzone and it is effectively invisible in dark. Lighten the dashed stroke substantially so the zone is legible.
- [ ] **Major** · dark · all widths — Dark mode helper captions ('Drag images into this area', 'Drag a file into this area') are dim gray on black, well below a comfortable contrast level and hard to read. Raise the muted-foreground token used in dark so secondary text stays legible.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · 1280px — At 1280 both dropzones are centered at ~600px with large empty margins on either side instead of filling their container. A dropzone is a spatial target and should adapt to available width; here it just floats in a mostly empty page rather than expanding.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Icon inconsistency between the two pickers: UploadFile's 'Choose File here' button carries an upload icon, while ImagePicker's 'Pick Images' button has none, and the ImagePicker dropzone has no illustrative icon at all. Two adjacent pickers should share the same icon language (e.g. an image/upload glyph centered in each empty zone).
- [ ] **Minor** · both · 360px — The two dropzones have noticeably different heights/aspect: ImagePicker is tall and squarish while UploadFile is short, so the stacked pair looks uneven and unbalanced at 360. Normalize their minimum heights.
- [ ] **Minor** · dark · all widths — Dark mode: the 'Pick Images' and 'Choose File here' buttons sit dark-gray-on-black inside an already dark dropzone with weak separation, so the primary action is easy to miss. Increase button surface contrast within the zone.
- [ ] **Polish** · both · all widths — No visible drag-over / hover active state or fill affordance is evident on the dropzones. Premium file pickers highlight (border + tint) on drag-over and show thumbnails/progress on drop; add a clear active state so the zone feels responsive.

## list — Grade F

- [ ] **Broken** · light+dark · 360+1280 — The entire list group fails to render. All four screenshots show a full-screen red 'Error 1 of 1' overlay instead of any list UI: 'ReanimatedError: [Reanimated] useAnimatedStyle was used without a dependency array or Babel plugin.' The call stack traces to a Chat component (main.js Chat -> useAnimatedStyle). No list content is visible at any theme or width. This is a hard crash from the reanimated web-support config (missing dependency array / Babel plugin on web), and it takes down the whole page. Nothing about the list group can be audited until this renders.
- [ ] **Broken** · light+dark · 360+1280 — Because the crash is identical in all four captures, the group has zero theme or responsive coverage. Even the error overlay itself is not theme-aware (same dark error card on the light-theme capture), so there is no fallback/empty state a user could recover from other than the 'Close' button.

## tables — Grade F

- [ ] **Broken** · light+dark · 360+1280 — The entire tables group fails to render. All four screenshots show the full-screen error overlay: 'Error: useGroupMedia: No parent group \'window\' found.' The call stack traces to BasicTable (main.js BasicTable -> useGroupMedia). BasicTable is calling a group-scoped media query (a `$group-window` / container-query grouping) without the required named group ('window') provider in the tree, so the component throws on mount. No table renders at any theme or width.
- [ ] **Broken** · light+dark · 360+1280 — This is a different root cause than the list crash (grouped-media context, not reanimated), so both need separate fixes. As with list, the crash is identical across themes/widths, meaning the tables group has no verifiable responsive or dark-mode behavior at all right now.

## preferences — Grade C

- [ ] **Major** · light+dark · 360+1280 — The section header renders as 'LOCATIONNOTIFICATION' — two section/tab labels ('Location' and 'Notification') are concatenated with zero spacing or separator, reading as one nonsense word. Present in all four captures. A premium library would show these as distinct, spaced eyebrow labels or a real segmented control with a gap/divider between them.
- [ ] **Major** · light+dark · 360+1280 — The Meeting card attendee avatars are broken: they render as the browser torn-photo 'broken image' placeholder icons (three of them, next to '+2') instead of user photos. Visible in all four captures. Either the avatar image URLs 404 or the local asset isn't bundled. Broken images in a showcase card read as clearly below the premium bar.
- [ ] **Minor** · light+dark · 1280px — At 1280 the eyebrow section labels ('LOCATION NOTIFICATION' and 'MEETING') are pinned to the far-left viewport edge (~x=170) while the form card and meeting cards are horizontally centered (card left edge ~x=400). The label and its content card do not share a left edge, so they look disconnected and the page has large empty gutters on both sides. Either left-align the cards under their labels or move the labels to align with the centered content column.
- [ ] **Minor** · dark · 360+1280 — In dark theme the three notification option cards (Promotions / The Weekly Update / Big Announcements) have near-invisible borders against the pure-black background, so the card separation and hierarchy nearly disappear; only the text distinguishes them. They read as floating text rather than distinct selectable rows. Raise the border/fill contrast (a subtle elevated surface) so the cards are legible as designed surfaces in dark, matching how they read in light.
- [ ] **Minor** · dark · 1280px — The thin horizontal divider rule that follows the 'LOCATION NOTIFICATION' and 'MEETING' eyebrow headers is barely perceptible in dark mode. It needs a slightly higher-contrast hairline so the section structure is visible on black.
- [ ] **Polish** · light+dark · 360+1280 — The subscription options use single-select radio controls (only 'Promotions' is filled, and the visuals imply only one can be chosen) for what reads semantically as independent email-subscription toggles. These should almost certainly be checkboxes or switches so a user can enable more than one. Worth confirming the intended interaction.
- [ ] **Polish** · light+dark · 1280px — At 1280 the form and meeting cards keep a narrow mobile-width column and simply center in a sea of whitespace rather than adapting to the wide viewport. It feels sparse/unintentional versus HeroUI Pro, which would either widen the content, add a two-column layout, or pair the form with a preview/summary panel to use the space deliberately.

## navbars — Grade D

- [ ] **Major** · both · all widths — TopNavBarWithLogo: the brand logo renders as a broken-image placeholder glyph (the classic missing-image mountain icon) in all four variants. At 1280 light it shows a stray 'R' fragment; at dark it's a white circle with the broken glyph. The logo asset is failing to load — a premium showcase cannot ship with a broken image in the hero nav slot.
- [ ] **Major** · both · 360px — TopNavBarWithLogo overflows horizontally at 360px. The link row (Products / People / Company / Blog / Contact) runs off the right edge and 'Company' is clipped to 'Compa', with Blog/Contact fully off-screen. There is no hamburger, wrap, or responsive collapse — the desktop layout is just shrunk, which is exactly the mobile failure HeroUI Pro avoids.
- [ ] **Major** · dark · all widths — FullSidebar: the group-header rows (Auth, User) use a filled highlight background that is nearly invisible in dark mode (near-black on black). The grouping/emphasis that reads clearly in light mode is lost, so the sidebar structure flattens into an undifferentiated list. Dark mode reads as inverted rather than designed-for.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — FullSidebar hierarchy is ambiguous: the Auth and User group headers use a solid filled-row treatment identical to what a selected/active item would use, so two rows appear simultaneously 'selected'. Section headers should be visually distinct from a selected nav item (weight/caps/color), and the sub-items (Sign In, Profile, etc.) carry no active-state indicator at all.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — TopNavBarWithLogo links (Products/People/Company/Blog/Contact) are rendered with a default text-underline, reading as raw unstyled anchor tags rather than a designed nav. No hover/press affordance is evident. Inconsistent with the underline-free link treatment used elsewhere.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · 1280px — FullSidebar right content panel: the vertical divider separating sidebar from content floats as a disconnected hairline that extends into a fully empty panel, and the top bar (avatar / notification bell) sits above blank space with no content framing. The empty right column makes the composition feel unfinished rather than intentionally minimal.
- [ ] **Polish** · both · all widths — FullSidebar 'Hi User!' avatar is a placeholder ghost glyph in a thin circle outline; combined with the broken logo and empty content panel, the navbar set reads as scaffolding rather than a polished, premium showcase. Real avatar art and populated content would lift the perceived quality.

## tabbars — Grade C

- [ ] **Major** · both · all widths — The 'TABBAR' example renders no visible tab bar at all — only the word 'Home' floats centered in a tall empty region. The actual bottom navigation (icons/labels row) that this example is meant to showcase is absent (not rendering or pushed off-frame), so the component's core artifact is invisible.
- [ ] **Minor** · both · all widths — Both examples have large stretches of unstructured vertical whitespace: 'Register' and 'Home' sit alone in tall blank areas with no card, panel, or content framing. It reads as empty/placeholder space rather than a deliberate layout, undercutting the premium feel.
- [ ] **Minor** · dark · all widths — TabBarSecondExample inactive labels (Purchase, Rest) are a low-contrast muted green/gray that is borderline legible in dark mode, and the active green (text + underline) is a single reused green that looks slightly washed on the dark background. The accent doesn't clearly derive from a theme token, so dark mode looks inverted rather than tuned.
- [ ] **Polish** · both · all widths — The tabs are bare text with a thin green underline and no hover/press affordance, background pill, or segmented-control container. Functional but generic versus a premium bar (no rest/hover/active depth, no touch-target padding cue), so it doesn't reach the HeroUI Pro polish bar.

## productpage — Grade F

- [ ] **Broken** · both · all widths — The entire productpage group crashes at runtime and renders only a red error overlay in all four variants: 'Error 1 of 1 — useGroupMedia: No parent group \'window\' found.' The call stack points at ProductWithReview calling useGroupMedia. The component references a media group named 'window' with no matching parent group provider, so React throws and nothing renders. This group is completely unusable and must be fixed before any visual audit is meaningful.

## animation-buttons — Grade F

- [ ] **Broken** · light+dark · 360+1280 — Entire group crashes at render in all four variants (light/dark x 360/1280) — only the dev error overlay shows, no button renders. TypeError: "Failed to set an indexed property [0] on 'CSSStyleDeclaration': Indexed property setter is not supported." Call stack: setValueForStyle -> setValueForStyles -> setProp -> setInitialProperties -> completeWork. A style prop is reaching a DOM host node as an array or an object with a numeric key (index 0), e.g. an un-flattened `style={[...]}` / transform array or an animation-driver style value that isn't being merged into a plain style object before hitting react-dom. Fix at the source: flatten/merge the style so no array or numeric-indexed value is passed to the DOM element.
- [ ] **Major** · light+dark · 360+1280 — Because it throws during commit (setInitialProperties/completeWork), there is no error boundary catching it — in production this becomes a blank/unusable page rather than an inline fallback. Wrap the showcase in an error boundary and verify the button actually mounts across all four animation drivers, since this style shape likely differs per driver (css/native/reanimated/motion).
